definition_zh: 珊瑚；珊瑚虫群体；珊瑚色；珊瑚制品
definition_en: a stony material built by tiny sea polyps, the animal colony itself, or the pink-orange colour of the precious kind
core_image: 海底一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，枝端还伸着细小的白色触手
scene: 浅海潜水时，向导指着一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，说明那些细小的触手是仍在取食的珊瑚虫。 The guide pointed to a branching pink-orange coral whose tiny polyps were still feeding.
sceneCN: 这里 coral 指「由珊瑚虫群体建造的活体珊瑚」（第 1 个义项：活着的珊瑚虫群体）；句意为向导指向一丛仍在取食的粉橙色枝状珊瑚。

derivatives.zh: 珊瑚的；珊瑚色的；珊瑚藻

senses.title: The living colony of polyps
senses.definition: a colony of small sea animals that build a shared skeleton around themselves
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细小海生动物构成的群体，它们在自己周围建造共同的骨骼
senses.example: The guide pointed to a branching coral whose polyps were still feeding.
senses.exampleCN: 向导指着一丛仍在取食的枝状珊瑚。
senses.why: Naturalists first took coral for a plant; once it was shown to be an animal, the same word came to name the living colony.
senses.whyCN: 博物学家最初把珊瑚当作植物；一旦证明它是动物，同一个词就开始指活的群体。

senses.title: The hard stony skeleton
senses.definition: the limy skeleton left by a coral colony, often branching or dome-shaped
senses.definitionCN: 珊瑚群体留下的钙质骨骼，常呈枝状或穹顶状
senses.example: The beach was made of broken coral and shell.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩由碎珊瑚和贝壳构成。
senses.why: The skeleton outlasts the animal, so the word transferred from the builder to the built thing.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼比动物活得久，于是这个词从建造者转到了被建造物上。

senses.title: The framework of a reef
senses.definition: coral as the main builder that raises a reef structure in shallow tropical seas
senses.definitionCN: 在浅热带海域抬升出礁体结构的主要造礁珊瑚
senses.example: Coral slowly raised a barrier along the edge of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚沿海岛边缘慢慢筑起一道堡礁。
senses.why: In geology coral names the construction material of the reef, not the animal that made it.
senses.whyCN: 在地质语境里，coral 指礁体的建筑材料，而不是造它的动物。

senses.title: Polished coral as a material
senses.definition: the hard red or pink coral cut and polished for use in objects
senses.definitionCN: 被切割打磨、用于制作器物的红色或粉色硬珊瑚
senses.example: The workshop set a piece of coral into a silver ring.
senses.exampleCN: 工坊把一块珊瑚嵌进银戒指。
senses.why: Once cut and polished, the skeleton becomes a gem-like material, and the word follows the trade.
senses.whyCN: 一旦切割打磨，骨骼就成了类宝石的材料，词义也随行业走。

senses.title: The orange-pink colour
senses.definition: a soft orange-pink colour like precious red coral
senses.definitionCN: 像贵重红珊瑚那样的柔和橙粉色
senses.example: The walls were painted a warm coral.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面被刷成温暖的珊瑚色。
senses.why: The colour name is a straightforward transfer: the hue is named after the object that supplied the dye-like shade.
senses.whyCN: 颜色名是直接的转喻：这种色调以提供它的物件命名。

senses.title: Coral as ornament
senses.definition: beads, carvings or jewellery made from coral
senses.definitionCN: 用珊瑚制成的珠子、雕件或首饰
senses.example: A string of coral hung at her throat.
senses.exampleCN: 她颈间挂着一串珊瑚。
senses.why: The material is metonymy for the finished object, a common path from stuff to ornament.
senses.whyCN: 材料转指成品，这是从「材质」到「饰物」的常见路径。

senses.title: Fossil coral in rock
senses.definition: the remains of ancient coral preserved in limestone or shale
senses.definitionCN: 保存在石灰岩或页岩中的古代珊瑚遗骸
senses.example: Fossil coral in the cliff shows that this desert was once a sea.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁里的珊瑚化石说明这片沙漠曾是海洋。
senses.why: Palaeontology keeps the name because the fossil keeps the shape, even though the animal is long gone.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学沿用这个名字，因为化石保留了形态，尽管动物早已消失。

senses.title: A protective talisman
senses.definition: red coral worn or hung as a charm against misfortune, especially for children
senses.definitionCN: 被佩戴或悬挂以避邪的红珊瑚，尤用于儿童
senses.example: The grandmother tied a small coral to the child's wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母把一小块珊瑚系在孩子手腕上。
senses.why: Traditional belief gave the red material a protective power, so coral also names a charm rather than a substance.
senses.whyCN: 传统信仰赋予红色材料护佑之力，因此 coral 也指护身符，而不只是物质。

intro.en: Coral reached English through Old French from Latin, which had borrowed the word from Greek; the Greek source is not fully settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coral 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，拉丁语又是从希腊语借来的；希腊语的来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Korallion was the name of the red coral of the Mediterranean. Its deeper origin is not established; a Semitic loan is a common hypothesis, not a proven fact.
items.cn: korallion 是地中海红珊瑚的名称。其更深来源没有定论；源自闪米特语是一种常见假说，并非已证事实。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as corallium and used it for the red skeletal material, which Romans carved into beads and charms.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 corallium，指红色的骨骼材料，罗马人把它雕成珠子和护符。

items.en: Old French coral carried the word into English in the twelfth century, at first for the precious red material rather than for a living animal.
items.cn: 古法语 coral 在 12 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指贵重的红色材料，而非活体动物。

items.en: For centuries coral was classed as a sea plant; eighteenth-century naturalists showed that the polyps are animals, and the zoological sense followed.
items.cn: 数百年来珊瑚被归为海生植物；18 世纪的博物学家证明珊瑚虫是动物，动物学义随之出现。

items.en: The colour name coral, for the soft orange-pink of the precious material, became common in English dress and decoration writing.
items.cn: 指贵重材料那种柔和橙粉色的颜色名 coral，在英语服饰与装饰文字中逐渐通行。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Greek korallion has no agreed etymology, and the Semitic Origin hypothesis is one proposal among several, so no single source is asserted here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：希腊 korallion 没有公认的词源，闪米特语来源只是若干假说之一，此处不武断选定一种。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same coral stock that are easily interchanged; group two holds reef and shell words with neighbouring meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 coral 词族、容易互换的词；第二组是意义相邻的礁与壳类词。

entries.definition: The plural counts colonies or kinds; coral as a mass material stays singular.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式计数群体或种类；作物质材料时仍用单数 coral。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of or like coral; as a noun it also names red coralline algae, a different organism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为珊瑚的或似珊瑚的；作名词时还指珊瑚藻，那是另一种生物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', so it describes a branching shape without claiming the material is coral.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，描述枝状形态，并不表示材料真是珊瑚。

entries.definition: A reef is the whole wave-resistant structure; coral is one builder within it, alongside algae and other organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 礁指整座抗浪结构；珊瑚只是其中的建造者之一，还有藻类及其他生物参与。

entries.definition: One coral animal is a polyp; coral names the colony and its skeleton, not the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 单个珊瑚动物叫 polyp；coral 指群体及其骨骼，而非单个个体。

entries.definition: A ridge of rock, sand or coral near the surface; it may be built by coral but need not be.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近水面的一道岩石、沙或珊瑚脊；它可以由珊瑚建造，但并非必然。

entries.definition: The hard outer case of a mollusc or other animal; coral is an internal skeleton built by a colony, not a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 软体动物等的外壳；珊瑚是群体建造的骨骼，不是外壳。

entries.definition: A rock made largely of calcium carbonate, often from coral and shell debris; it is the stone, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 主要由碳酸钙构成的岩石，常来自珊瑚与贝壳碎屑；它指岩石，不指动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Coral names both the animal colony and the stone it leaves behind, so context decides which is meant.
normal.cn: coral 既指活体群体，也指它留下的石头，靠上下文判断指哪一个。

normal.en: The colour coral is simply the colour of red coral, not a separate root.
normal.cn: 颜色义 coral 就是红珊瑚的颜色，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Coral reef and coral island are fixed compounds; reef alone can be rock or sand.
normal.cn: coral reef 与 coral island 是固定复合词；单说 reef 则可能是岩礁或沙洲。

normal.en: Coralline and coralloid both start with coral but point to 'of coral' and 'like coral' respectively.
normal.cn: coralline 与 coralloid 都以 coral 开头，但分别指「珊瑚的」与「像珊瑚的」。

normal.en: Coral bleaching is the fixed phrase for the whitening that follows the loss of algal partners.
normal.cn: 珊瑚失去共生藻后变白，固定说法是 coral bleaching。

abstract.en: Picture a city built by animals that never leave home, each adding a room of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由从不离家的动物建起的城市，每只都添一间石屋。

abstract.en: Picture a pink branch that is soft while alive and becomes jewellery when dead.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粉色的枝，活着时柔软，死后变成首饰。

abstract.en: Picture a desert cliff holding the shape of a sea that vanished.
abstract.cn: 想象一面沙漠崖壁里留着早已消失的海洋的形状。

examples.en: Coral grows only where the water stays warm and clear.
examples.cn: 珊瑚只在水温温暖、水质清澈的地方生长。

examples.en: The island is a ring of coral around a drowned crater.
examples.cn: 这座岛是一圈环绕着沉没火山口的珊瑚。

examples.en: She chose a coral dress for the summer wedding.
examples.cn: 她为夏季婚礼选了一条珊瑚色的裙子。

dict_mnemonic.text: coral 读起来像「口若」——珊瑚枝一条条张开小口，像在不停地开口吃东西

root: 希腊 korallion「红珊瑚」→ 拉丁 corallium → 古法语 coral；korallion 的更深来源不确定，闪米特语来源只是一种假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object from life to stone to symbol: the living colony, its skeleton, the reef it raises, the polished material, the colour, the ornament, the fossil, and the charm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一物件从生命走到石头再走到象征：活体群体、骨骼、抬升的礁、打磨的材料、颜色、饰品、化石与护符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pink branching stone with tiny white tentacles at the tips.
core.cn: 核心意象：粉色的枝状石头，枝端伸出细小的白色触手。

branches.en: BUILDER AND BUILT: the colony makes the stone, then the stone outlasts the colony.
branches.cn: 建造者与被建造物：群体造出石头，石头又比群体活得久。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION: in geology the material is the reef itself.
branches.cn: 建筑：在地质语境中，这种材料就是礁体。

branches.en: MATERIAL TO ORNAMENT: cutting and polishing turn skeleton into gem and then into jewellery.
branches.cn: 从材料到饰品：切割打磨把骨骼变成宝石，再变成首饰。

branches.en: COLOUR BY METONYMY: the hue is named directly after the precious red kind.
branches.cn: 转喻得色：色调直接以贵重的红珊瑚命名。

branches.en: FROM STONE TO SYMBOL: the fossil proves an ancient sea, the charm promises protection.
branches.cn: 从石到象征：化石证明古海，护符许诺护佑。

intro.en: Coral is a borrowed noun with no productive English prefix; its family is built by compounding and by the suffixes -ine and -oid.
intro.cn: coral 是借入名词，没有能产的英语前缀；其词族靠复合与后缀 -ine、-oid 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin corallium and Greek korallion are the source forms; corallum is the Latin noun used in natural history for a coral colony.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 corallium 与希腊 korallion 是来源形式；corallum 是博物学中用于指珊瑚群体的拉丁名词。

items.meaning: red coral, and later any coral
items.meaningCN: 红珊瑚；后泛指各类珊瑚
items.example: Coral was once classed as a plant.
The reef holds hundreds of corals.

items.meaning: of coral; also a red coralline alga
items.example: Coralline algae cement the reef frame.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚藻把礁体胶结起来。

items.example: The suffix marks resemblance, not identity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记相似，而非同一。
这种矿物形成珊瑚状的枝。

items.meaning: a reef built chiefly by coral
items.example: The coral reef shelters the lagoon.

items.meaning: an island made largely of coral
items.example: Coral islands rise only a few metres above the sea.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚岛只高出海面几米。

items.example: The corallum is the whole skeletal frame.

definition_zh: 细绳；电线；索带
definition_en: a thick string, an electrical wire with a cover, or a cord-like part of the body
core_image: 一根细绳绕在手上，勒出浅浅的痕
scene: 包裹摊在桌上，他找出一根绳子把它系紧。He tied the parcel with a thin cord.
sceneCN: 这里 cord 指「细绳」（第 1 个义项：较粗的绳子）；句意是他用一根细绳把包裹捆好。

senses.title: A thick string
senses.definition: a length of thick string made of twisted threads
senses.definitionCN: 由多股线捻成的较粗绳子
senses.example: She hung the curtain with a silk cord.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一根丝绳挂起窗帘。
senses.why: Twisting many weak threads makes one strong line.
senses.whyCN: 把许多细弱的线捻在一起，就成了一条结实的线。

senses.title: An electrical cable
senses.definition: a covered wire that carries electricity to a device
senses.definitionCN: 把电送到电器的包皮导线
senses.example: The lamp cord was too short.
senses.exampleCN: 台灯的电线太短了。
senses.why: Power also needs a path, and the path is named like a string.
senses.whyCN: 电也需要一条路，而这条路就用绳子的名字来叫。

senses.title: A cord-like body part
senses.definition: a long thin part of the body that looks like a cord
senses.definitionCN: 身体中细长如绳的部分
senses.example: The spinal cord carries signals from the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 脊髓把信号从大脑传出去。
senses.why: Inside the body, nerves also travel in long twisted bundles.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部，神经也是成束地长距离行走。

intro.en: Cord comes from Greek khorde, a string of gut, through Latin chorda and Old French corde.
intro.cn: cord 来自希腊语 khorde（肠弦），经拉丁语 chorda 与古法语 corde 进入英语。

items.en: Khorde meant a string made from animal gut.
items.cn: khorde 意为用动物肠子做的弦。

items.en: Chorda named a string for a musical instrument.
items.cn: chorda 指乐器的弦。

items.en: Old French corde widened the sense to any strong string.
items.cn: 古法语 corde 把词义扩大到任何结实的绳子。

items.en: English cord named rope used in daily work.
items.cn: 英语 cord 指日常劳作所用的绳。

items.en: Electricity gave the word the sense of a covered wire.
items.cn: 电的应用让这个词获得了包皮电线的含义。

items.en: The body sense survives in spinal cord and vocal cords.
items.cn: 身体义项保留在 spinal cord 与 vocal cords 中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin string base cord-, and the meaning group names other things that tie or carry power.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的弦词基 cord-，近义组列出其他用于捆扎或导电的东西。

entries.definition: several musical notes played together
an official agreement between sides
friendly and warm in manner
a very strong thick cord
a thin cord used for tying
a thin metal thread for power

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with twisted threads in a hand, then move to a lamp cable and to the spine.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从手里捻起的细线开始，再到台灯的电线，最后到脊柱。

normal.en: Cord and chord sound the same but live in different worlds: one ties, one sings.
normal.cn: cord 与 chord 读音相同却分居两界：一个捆东西，一个唱歌。

normal.en: Twist several threads and you get a cord; twist many cords and you get a rope.
normal.cn: 几股线捻起来是 cord，许多 cord 再捻起来就是 rope。

normal.en: A lamp cord is just a string that carries power.
normal.cn: 台灯的电线，不过是一根送电的绳子。

normal.en: The spinal cord is a cord inside the backbone.
normal.cn: 脊髓就是脊柱里的一根索带。

normal.en: The -less form, cordless, means free of that string.
normal.cn: 加 -less 的 cordless，就是摆脱了那根线。

abstract.en: Picture three threads twisted into one line.
abstract.cn: 想象三股线被捻成一条。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp cord curling across a wooden floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一根灯线弯曲着铺在木地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a long white cord running down a spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的白色索带沿脊柱而下。

examples.en: She cut a length of cord to tie the box.
examples.cn: 她剪了一截细绳来捆箱子。

examples.en: Unplug the cord before you move the lamp.
examples.cn: 搬动台灯之前先拔掉电线。

examples.en: Damage to the spinal cord can be serious.
examples.cn: 脊髓受损可能很严重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cord 记成几股线拧成的一根：能捆东西的是绳，能送电的是线，长在身体里的是索。

root: 源自希腊语 khorde（肠弦），经拉丁语 chorda（琴弦）与古法语 corde 进入英语，由琴弦引申为细绳、电线与索状组织。

sensesIntro.en: From a twisted string, to a cable carrying power, and at last to a cord inside the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从捻成的细绳，到输送电力的电线，最后到身体里的一根索带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin cord wound around a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细绳绕在手上。

branches.en: Twisted threads make a line strong enough to tie.
branches.cn: 捻起的线做成一条足够结实的捆扎线。

branches.en: A covered line carries power to a machine.
branches.cn: 包皮的线把电送到机器上。

branches.en: A cord in the body carries signals instead of current.
branches.cn: 身体里的索带传的是信号，不是电流。

branches.en: Both are long flexible lines with a job.
branches.cn: 两者都是有任务的长而柔韧的线。

branches.en: Power and nerve both travel along a named path.
branches.cn: 电力与神经都沿着一条有名字的路径行走。

intro.en: Cord comes from Latin chorda, a string, and forms corded, cordless and cording in English.
intro.cn: cord 来自拉丁语 chorda（弦），在英语里构成 corded、cordless 与 cording。

latinIntro.en: The string base cord- also appears in chord, accord and cordial.
latinIntro.cn: 弦词基 cord- 也出现在 chord、accord 与 cordial 中。

items.exampleCN: 她弹了一个柔和的弦音。
一场热情的欢迎等着我们。

items.meaning: a line of people or posts guarding an area
items.meaningCN: 围住某区域的人墙或警戒线
items.exampleCN: 一道警戒线封住了街道。

definition_zh: adj. 热诚的，热情友好的；n. 甘露酒
definition_en: warm and friendly, or a sweet fruit drink
core_image: 主人伸出手，满脸笑意地把客人迎进门
scene: 主人热情地迎接每一位来访的客人。The host gave every guest a cordial welcome.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cordial 指热诚的；句意是主人热情迎接每位客人。

senses.title: Warm and friendly
senses.definition: warm and pleasant in manner
senses.definitionCN: 态度温暖亲切
senses.example: They gave us a cordial welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 他们热情地欢迎我们。
senses.why: A hand held out with a smile.
senses.whyCN: 笑着伸出的手。

senses.title: Heartfelt
senses.definition: sincere and deeply felt
senses.definitionCN: 真诚而深切
senses.example: He offered cordial thanks.
senses.exampleCN: 他由衷地道谢。
senses.why: Words said from the chest, not the lips.
senses.whyCN: 从心里说出的话。

senses.title: A sweet drink
senses.definition: a sweet fruit drink or liqueur
senses.definitionCN: 甜味果汁或利口酒

definition_zh: 公司的；法人的；团体的；共同组成的
definition_en: relating to a corporation or a large business, or shared by all members of a group
core_image: 许多人被铸成同一个法人身体
scene: 新员工在宣传片里看到同一栋大楼、同一句口号。 In the new recruitment film the staff saw the same tower, the same slogan, and the same corporate logo.
sceneCN: 这里 corporate 是「公司的」（第 1 个义项：与公司有关的）；句意：在新宣传片里，员工看到同一栋大楼、同一句口号和同一个公司标志。

senses.title: Relating to a business corporation
senses.definition: connected with a corporation or a large company rather than an individual
senses.definitionCN: 与公司或大企业有关，而不是与个人有关
senses.example: The company moved its corporate headquarters downtown.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把总部搬到了市中心。
senses.why: corporate is Latin corpus 'body' + -ate. A corporation is a group legally treated as one body, so corporate describes whatever belongs to that body.
senses.whyCN: corporate 是拉丁语 corpus“身体”+ -ate。corporation 是被法律当作一个身体看待的群体，因此 corporate 描述属于这个身体的一切。

senses.title: Of large companies as a social force
senses.titleCN: 作为社会力量的大企业
senses.definition: relating to big business as a political, cultural, or economic power
senses.definitionCN: 与作为政治、文化或经济力量的大企业有关
senses.example: The film criticises corporate power.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片批评企业权力。
senses.why: When a legal body grows large, it acts almost like a person with interests. Corporate then names the collective actor, not just its paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当一个法律身体变大，它几乎像一个有利益的人那样行动。corporate 此时命名的是集体行动者，而不只是它的文件。

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: belonging to or shared by all members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 属于或由群体全体成员共同拥有
senses.example: The report is a corporate effort, not one person's work.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是集体努力的结果，不是一个人的工作。
senses.why: The 'one body' image makes authorship collective. A corporate effort comes from the body as a whole, even if many hands made it.
senses.whyCN: “一个身体”的意象使作者身份变成集体的。集体努力来自整个身体，即使有许多只手参与。

senses.title: United in one legal body
senses.definition: in legal and historical usage, formed into a single body with legal personality
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与历史用法中，组成具有法人人格的单一团体
senses.example: The bishops met as a corporate body.
senses.exampleCN: 主教们以一个法人团体的身份开会。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a group is 'bodied' into one entity that can hold property and act in law. The body is not physical but legal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最老的义项：一群人被“结成身体”，成为一个能持有财产、在法律上行动的实体。这个身体不是物理的，而是法律的。

senses.title: Of corporate law, finance, and governance
senses.titleCN: 公司法、金融与治理层面的
senses.definition: relating to the legal and financial structure of companies, such as boards, shares, and mergers
senses.definitionCN: 与公司的法律和财务结构有关，如董事会、股份和并购
senses.example: Corporate law governs mergers and acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 公司法规范并购活动。
senses.why: A legal body needs organs and rules: a board, shareholders, meetings. Corporate marks the level at which the body itself, not its employees, is the subject.
senses.whyCN: 法律身体需要器官和规则：董事会、股东、会议。corporate 标记的是“身体本身”而非员工作为行为主体的层级。

senses.title: Corporate identity and branding
senses.definition: relating to the visual and verbal identity a company presents to the public
senses.definitionCN: 与公司向公众呈现的视觉和语言识别系统有关
senses.example: They redesigned the corporate logo and colours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们重新设计了公司标志和配色。
senses.why: A body needs a face. The logo, typeface and slogan give the collective body one recognisable appearance.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要一张脸。标志、字体和口号给这个集体身体一个可辨认的外观。

senses.title: Of a municipality or other incorporated body
senses.definition: relating to any group given legal personality, such as a city or a charity
senses.definitionCN: 与任何被赋予法人资格的群体有关，如城市或慈善机构
senses.example: The city is a corporate entity with its own powers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是一个拥有自身权力的法人实体。
senses.why: Incorporation is not limited to business. A city, university or charity can also be one body in law, and corporate describes that status.
senses.whyCN: 法人化并不限于商业。城市、大学或慈善机构也可以在法律上成为一个身体，corporate 描述的就是这种身份。

senses.title: Derived family: corporation and corporatism
senses.definition: in corporation and corporatism, the 'body' image is applied to a company or to a state organised by occupational groups
senses.definitionCN: 在 corporation 与 corporatism 中，“身体”意象被用于公司，或被用于按职业团体组织起来的国家
senses.example: Corporatism builds an economy out of corporate bodies such as guilds and employers' groups.
senses.exampleCN: 社团主义用行会、雇主团体这类法人团体来搭建经济。
senses.why: The same body image produces very different institutions: a company, a city, or a state built from occupational corporations. The suffix changes, the body stays.
senses.whyCN: 同一个身体意象产生很不同的制度：公司、城市，或由职业团体构成的国家。后缀变了，身体还在。

intro.en: Corporate comes from corpus 'body'. A corporation is a group made into one legal body, and corporate describes anything belonging to that body — business, city, or state.
intro.cn: corporate 来自 corpus“身体”。corporation 是被制成一个法律身体的群体，corporate 描述属于这个身体的一切——企业、城市或国家。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'united in one body'. The commercial sense 'of a business corporation' develops later.
items.cn: 15 世纪最早记录，意为“结成一体”。“属于商业公司”的义项后来才发展出来。

items.en: From Latin corporatus, past participle of corporare 'to form into a body', from corpus 'body'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 corporatus，即 corporare“使成为身体”的过去分词，后者来自 corpus“身体”。

items.en: corpus (genitive corporis) 'body' is traced to PIE *kwrep- 'body, form, appearance'; the reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: corpus（属格 corporis）“身体”被追溯到原始印欧语 *kwrep-“身体、形体、外观”；该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: The adjective corporate attaches to corporations and incorporated bodies. In the 19c. it becomes the everyday adjective of large business.
items.cn: 形容词 corporate 与 corporation 及法人团体绑定。19 世纪它成为大企业的日常形容词。

items.en: Corporate culture, corporate governance and corporate identity appear as management vocabulary; corporatism names a state organised by occupational bodies.
items.cn: corporate culture、corporate governance、corporate identity 作为管理词汇出现；corporatism 指按职业团体组织起来的国家。

items.en: Modern English uses corporate mainly as an adjective. The noun is corporation, and the verb incorporate keeps the literal 'put into a body'.
items.cn: 现代英语主要把 corporate 用作形容词。名词是 corporation，动词 incorporate 保留字面义“放进一个身体里”。

note.en: The first group shares corpus 'body'; the second group separates business, collective, institutional and commercial meanings.
note.cn: 第一组共享 corpus“身体”；第二组区分商业、集体、制度和营利这几种含义。

entries.definition: relating to the body, especially physical punishment. It comes from corpus but means 'bodily', not 'of a company'.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的，尤指体罚。它来自 corpus，但意思是“身体的”，不是“公司的”。

entries.definition: having a physical body; tangible. It is the philosophical cousin of corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 有实体的；物质的。它是 corporate 的哲学近亲。

entries.definition: to include something as part of a whole, or to form a legal corporation.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物纳入整体，或组成法人公司。

entries.definition: related to buying and selling for profit. It focuses on trade, while corporate focuses on the legal body.
entries.definitionCN: 与营利性买卖有关。它聚焦交易，而 corporate 聚焦法律实体。

entries.definition: shared by a group. It is broader than corporate and does not imply a legal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 群体共同拥有的。它比 corporate 更宽泛，不暗示法律结构。

entries.definition: relating to an established organisation such as a university, bank, or hospital. It is wider than corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与大学、银行、医院等已建立的组织有关。它比 corporate 范围更广。

entries.definition: relating to trade or a company, used before nouns such as business plan. It is plainer and less legal than corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与交易或公司有关，用于 business plan 等名词前。它比 corporate 更日常、更少法律色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: corpus 'body' + -ate 'made'. Corporation, corpse, corps, corporal and incorporate all belong to the body family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：corpus“身体”+ -ate“使成为”。corporation、corpse、corps、corporal、incorporate 都属于“身体”词族。

normal.en: corpus means body. A corporation is a group given one legal body, and corporate means belonging to that body.
normal.cn: corpus 意为身体。corporation 是被赋予一个法律身体的群体，corporate 表示属于这个身体。

normal.en: Corpse, corps, corporal and incorporate all contain the body idea: a dead body, a body of troops, bodily, and put into a body.
normal.cn: corpse、corps、corporal、incorporate 都含“身体”：尸体、军队团体、身体的、纳入身体。

normal.en: A corporate logo is the face of the legal body; corporate law is its skeleton.
normal.cn: 公司标志是法律身体的脸；公司法是它的骨架。

normal.en: Corporate culture is the personality of the body, the habits its members share.
normal.cn: 企业文化就是这个身体的性格，是成员共享的习惯。

normal.en: Incorporate means 'put into the body', whether a clause into a contract or a business into a legal form.
normal.cn: incorporate 意为“放进身体里”，无论是把条款放进合同，还是把企业放进法律形式。

abstract.en: Imagine hundreds of employees welded into one silhouette. The silhouette signs contracts, owns buildings and speaks through one logo.
abstract.cn: 想象几百名员工被焊成一个人形轮廓。这个轮廓签合同、拥有大楼，并通过一个标志说话。

abstract.en: A corporation is a body without a heartbeat: it needs a board as its brain and a charter as its spine.
abstract.cn: 公司是一个没有心跳的身体：它需要董事会当大脑、章程当脊柱。

abstract.en: The same body image can be small as a shop or large as a state; only the scale of the silhouette changes.
abstract.cn: 同一个身体意象可以小到一家店铺，大到一个国家；变的只是轮廓的大小。

examples.en: The bank announced a major corporate restructuring.
examples.cn: 这家银行宣布了大规模的公司重组。

examples.en: Corporate responsibility includes how suppliers treat their workers.
examples.cn: 企业责任包括供应商如何对待工人。

examples.en: The city acts as a corporate body when it signs the contract.
examples.cn: 这座城市签署合同时，是以法人团体的身份行事。

root: 拉丁语 corpus“身体”+ -ate，字面义“结成一体”，核心是“许多人合成一个法律上的身体”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of corporate, all one legal body: a company, a social power, a shared effort, a body in law, its law and finance, its face, a city, and the derived institutions built on the image.
sensesIntro.cn: corporate 的八个义项都是同一个法律身体：公司、社会力量、共同出力、法律上的团体、法律与财务、对外的脸、城市，以及由这个意象衍生的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many people are formed into a single body that can act in law.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多人被铸成一个能在法律上行动的身体。

branches.en: COMPANY: the body as a business and as a legal-financial structure.
branches.cn: 公司：作为企业、也作为法律—财务结构的身体。

branches.en: PUBLIC FACE: a large body with power, and a body with a logo.
branches.cn: 公众面孔：拥有权力的大身体，以及带着标志的身体。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE: work and authorship belong to the body, not one hand.
branches.cn: 集体：工作与署名属于身体，而不属于某一只手。

branches.en: LEGAL STATUS: bishops, cities and charities can all be one body.
branches.cn: 法律身份：主教团、城市、慈善机构都可以是一个身体。

branches.en: DERIVED INSTITUTIONS: corporation and corporatism extend the body to economy and state.
branches.cn: 衍生制度：corporation 与 corporatism 把身体扩展到经济与国家。

intro.en: Corporate takes corpus and the suffix -ate 'made, formed'. English builds corporation with -ion and incorpor- with in-. The body image is carried by the suffix change.
intro.cn: corporate 由 corpus 加后缀 -ate“使成为”构成。英语用 -ion 构成 corporation，用 in- 构成 incorpor-。身体意象随着后缀变化被带到新词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on corpus 'body': corpse, corps, corporal, corporeal and incorporate all describe a body or the putting of something into one.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 corpus“身体”上：corpse、corps、corporal、corporeal、incorporate 都描述身体，或把某物放进一个身体。

items.meaning: a company or group legally treated as a single body
items.meaningCN: 公司；法人团体（-ion 构成结果名词）

definition_zh: （使）相关；使相互关联；对应；并置比对
definition_en: to have a mutual relation, or to place two sets of things so that they match
core_image: 两条曲线画在同一张方格纸上，一条升高时另一条也跟着升高，起落彼此对齐
scene: 研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量并排画在同一张图上，两条线几乎同步起落。Researchers correlate rainfall records with river flow over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里指把两组记录并排摆放，使对应项彼此对齐（第 5 个义项：把两组数据或记录对齐比对）；句意：研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量对应起来看。

senses.title: Of two things varying together
senses.definition: of two quantities or facts, to change together in a way that can be observed
senses.definitionCN: 指两个数量或事实以可观察的方式一同变化
senses.example: Height and weight correlate across the whole population.
senses.exampleCN: 在整个人群中，身高与体重是相关的。
senses.why: The prefix means together and the root means carried back, so two things are carried back to each other.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示一起，词根表示带回，因此两样东西彼此被带回对照。

senses.title: To show a statistical correlation
senses.definition: to establish by measurement that two variables move together more than chance would explain
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量确定两个变量的同向变化超出偶然所能解释的范围
senses.example: The survey correlates income with years of schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把收入与受教育年限联系起来。
senses.why: Statistics turned the mutual relation into a coefficient, and the verb took on the measuring sense.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把相互关联变成一个系数，这个动词也就有了测量的含义。

senses.title: To connect things in the mind
senses.titleCN: 在心里把事物联系起来
senses.definition: to bring two ideas into a mental link so that one calls up the other
senses.definitionCN: 把两个观念在心里连起来，使一个能唤起另一个
senses.example: Children correlate the sound of the bell with the end of class.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把铃声与下课联系起来。
senses.why: The mind carries one idea back to another, which is the same movement the Latin root names.
senses.whyCN: 心智把一个观念带回另一个，这正是那个拉丁词根所命名的动作。

senses.title: To correspond to each other
senses.definition: of two series or accounts, to match item by item so that each has a partner
senses.definitionCN: 指两个序列或两份陈述逐项吻合，各自都有对应项
senses.example: The numbered seals correlate with the entries in the catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 带编号的印章与目录中的条目一一对应。
senses.why: The preposition with marks the second term of the pair, and the verb simply reports that the pair fits.
senses.whyCN: 介词标明这一对中的第二项，动词只报告这一对彼此吻合。

senses.title: To line up two sets of records
senses.definition: to arrange two sets of data or documents so that matching items stand side by side
senses.definitionCN: 把两组数据或文件排列好，使相配的项目彼此并排
senses.example: Researchers correlate rainfall records with river flow over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量对应起来看。
senses.why: Records are correlated when one column is laid against another, which is the manual act behind the statistics.
senses.whyCN: 当一列数据对着另一列摆好，记录就被对齐了，这是统计背后的手工动作。

senses.title: To match rock layers across regions
senses.titleCN: 把不同地区的岩层对应起来
senses.definition: in geology, to identify layers in separate places as the same age or origin
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学中，判定不同地点的地层属于同一时代或同一来源
senses.example: Geologists correlate the sandstone beds on both sides of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家把河谷两侧的砂岩层对应起来。
senses.why: Strata are matched by their fossils and grain, the same lining-up act carried out on a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 地层靠化石与颗粒特征配对，就是把对齐动作放到整片地貌上。

senses.title: Of traits that vary together in species
senses.definition: in biology, of two traits or structures, to occur together across related organisms
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指两种性状或结构在亲缘生物中相伴出现
senses.example: Wing length and body size correlate in these birds.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些鸟身上，翅长与体型大小是相关的。
senses.why: Living things supply paired measurements too, so the statistical sense extends to natural variation.
senses.whyCN: 生物同样提供成对的测量值，统计义便延伸到自然变异。

senses.title: To compare findings across studies
senses.titleCN: 在多项研究之间做对应比较
senses.definition: to bring results from separate studies into one comparison so that agreement or conflict shows
senses.definitionCN: 把不同研究的结果放进同一次比较，使一致或冲突之处显现
senses.example: The review correlates the findings of twelve field studies.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇综述把十二项实地研究的发现对应比较。
senses.why: Research synthesis is a large-scale version of laying two records side by side.
senses.whyCN: 研究综合就是把两份记录并排摆放这一动作的放大版。

intro.en: Correlate joins a prefix meaning together to the Latin participle of the verb for carrying back. Medieval Latin used the pair for things that answer to each other, and statistics gave the word its modern measuring sense.
intro.cn: 本词把表示一起的前缀接在拉丁语中表示带回的动词分词上。中世纪拉丁语用这一对词指彼此呼应之物，统计学又给了它现代的测量含义。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back or to bring into relation, and its participle is the second half of this word.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为带回或使发生关联，它的分词就是本词的后半截。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together, so the compound said carried back together, that is, set in a mutual relation.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起，因此复合词意为被一起带回，也就是被摆进相互关系。

items.en: Medieval Latin used the form for things that correspond, especially in grammar and theology.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用这个形式指彼此对应之物，尤其见于语法与神学。

items.en: Nineteenth-century statistics made correlation a measured relation between two variables.
items.cn: 十九世纪的统计学把相关变成两个变量之间可测量的关系。

items.en: English took the verb in the nineteenth century, chiefly in scientific and academic writing.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个动词，主要用于科学与学术写作。

items.en: Geology, biology and research synthesis later applied the same alignment to strata, traits and whole studies.
items.cn: 地质学、生物学与研究综合后来把同一种对齐动作用于地层、性状与整项研究。

note.en: The first group shares the carrying-back root or its family forms; the second group names nearby kinds of matching. Correlate reports that two things vary or line up together, while corroborate reports that evidence makes a claim stronger, so relation and proof must not be confused.
note.cn: 第一组共享带回词根或其词族形式；第二组是相邻的配对类型。本词说的是两件事一同变化或彼此对齐，佐证类词说的是证据把某个说法坐实，关系与证明不能混为一谈。

entries.definition: The measured relation between two things, or the act of aligning them.

entries.definition: Mutually related, and in grammar a paired word such as either and or.

entries.definition: Considered in relation to something else; it stops short of measuring a pair.

entries.definition: To connect or to tell; it is the plainer verb behind the noun.

entries.definition: To match or to exchange letters; matching is by form or position, not by measured variation.
entries.definitionCN: 相配或通信；匹配依据形式或位置，而非测量出的共同变化。

entries.definition: To link in thought or in company; no measurement is implied.
entries.definitionCN: 在思想上或交往中联系；不牵涉测量。

entries.definition: To join or to show a link; it is the general word for any linkage.
entries.definitionCN: 连接或显示联系；是任何联系的泛称。

entries.definition: To put two things together because they are alike; the judgement is identity, not variation.
entries.definitionCN: 因相似而把两物配在一起；判断的是相同，而非共变。

entries.definition: To fall on the same point or time; coincidence is exact, correlation is statistical.
entries.definitionCN: 落在同一点或同一时刻；重合是精确的，相关是统计的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the carrying-back root, the real family and the preposition that marks the second term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用带回词根、真实同族词，以及标记第二项的介词。

normal.en: The root means carried back, so two things are carried back to each other for comparison.
normal.cn: 词根意为带回，两样东西被带回到彼此面前作比较。

normal.en: The family runs correlation, correlative, correlated and correlational.
normal.cn: 同族词有相关、对应的、相关的与相关性研究的。

normal.en: The preposition is with: one thing correlates with another.
normal.cn: 介词用与：一事物与另一事物相关。

normal.en: Statistics supplies the number, but the everyday sense needs no number at all.
normal.cn: 统计学提供数值，但日常义完全不需要数值。

normal.en: The geological sense is a large-scale version: whole layers matched across a valley.
normal.cn: 地质义是放大版：整层岩层跨越河谷彼此对应。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers who never touch but always turn at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名舞者从不接触，却总在同一瞬间转身。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks in different rooms that keep the same error.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间里的两只钟犯着同样的误差。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that lengthens exactly as the person grows.
abstract.cn: 想象影子随着人的长高而变长。

examples.en: Income does not always correlate with happiness.
examples.cn: 收入并不总与幸福感相关。

examples.en: The two lists correlate neatly once the dates are aligned.
examples.cn: 把日期对齐之后，两份清单便整齐地对应起来。

examples.en: Researchers correlate soil acidity with crop yield.
examples.cn: 研究者把土壤酸度与作物产量对应起来分析。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可」加「瑞」加「累特」——两条线一起起落，像被同一根绳拉着：相关

root: 拉丁语「带回」动词的分词加「一起」前缀，中世纪拉丁语指彼此对应之物，十九世纪经统计学获得「相关」的测量含义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one alignment: variables varying together, a measured coefficient, mental association, item-by-item matching, records laid side by side, rock layers, paired traits and pooled studies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种对齐：变量共同变化、测出的系数、心里的联想、逐项对应、并排的记录、岩层、成对的性状，以及汇总的研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves drawn on one sheet of graph paper, rising and falling together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条曲线画在同一张方格纸上，一条升高时另一条也跟着升高，起落彼此对齐。

branches.en: THE MEASURED RELATION: things varying together, and the coefficient that records it.
branches.cn: 被测量的关系：事物共同变化，以及记录它的系数。

branches.en: THE MIND: one idea calling up another without any number.
branches.cn: 心智：一个观念唤起另一个，不涉及数值。

branches.en: THE ALIGNMENT: series corresponding item by item, and records laid side by side.
branches.cn: 对齐：序列逐项对应，记录并排摆放。

branches.en: THE NATURAL WORLD: rock layers matched across a valley and traits paired across a species.
branches.cn: 自然世界：跨越河谷对应的岩层，以及物种中成对的性状。

branches.en: THE LITERATURE: separate studies brought into one comparison.
branches.cn: 文献：多项研究被放进同一次比较。

intro.en: Correlate is a Latin compound of togetherness and carrying back, and its family supplies the noun, the adjective and the plainer verb of relation.
intro.cn: 本词是表示「一起」与「带回」的拉丁复合词，其词族提供名词、形容词，以及更平实的关联动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin referre and its participle relatus supply the second half; com- supplies the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示带回的动词及其分词提供后半截，前缀提供前半截。

items.example: The verb supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供复合词的后半截。

items.example: The participle is the shape English actually took over.
items.exampleCN: 英语实际接收的是这个分词形式。

items.example: Medieval writers added the prefix to the participle.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪作者在这个分词前加了前缀。

items.example: It turns the Latin stem into the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干变成英语动词。

items.example: It builds the name of the measured relation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被测量关系的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for paired items.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述成对项目的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for studies of correlation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述相关性研究的形容词。

items.example: The pair needs this preposition to name its second term.
items.exampleCN: 这一对需要这个介词引出第二项。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry back, to bring into relation

definition_zh: 关联；相关；相互关系
definition_en: a connection or relationship between two or more things, especially one where one changes as the other changes
core_image: 两条线一起起伏，步调呼应
scene: 这组词中，The study found a strong correlation between exercise and mental health.
sceneCN: 这里 correlation 是「关联」（第 1 个义项：两事物之间的联系）；句意：研究发现运动与心理健康之间存在强关联。图中可辨识物件：坐标图、两条同步起伏的曲线、放大镜。

senses.title: A connection between two things
senses.definition: a connection or relationship between two or more things
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多事物之间的联系或关系
senses.example: There is a correlation between smoking and lung cancer.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟与肺癌之间存在关联。
senses.why: Latin referre 'to carry back' → relatio 'relation' + cor- (com-): correlation is a 'together relation'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 referre「带回」→ relatio「关系」+ cor-（com-）：correlation 是「一起的关系」。

senses.title: A measure of how things vary together
senses.definition: in statistics, a measure of the extent to which two variables change together
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中，两个变量一起变化程度的度量
senses.example: The correlation between height and weight is high.
senses.exampleCN: 身高和体重之间的相关度很高。
senses.why: In statistics, correlation quantifies how closely two sets of data move together.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学中，correlation 量化两组数据一起变动的紧密程度。

senses.title: A mutual relationship
senses.definition: a relationship in which two things affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 两事物相互影响的关系
senses.example: The correlation between stress and illness is complex.
senses.exampleCN: 压力与疾病之间的相互关系很复杂。
senses.why: When two things are correlated, they vary in a related way, though one may not cause the other.
senses.whyCN: 当两事物相关时，它们以相关的方式变化，尽管不一定有因果关系。

senses.title: A correspondence between sets
senses.definition: a matching or correspondence between elements of different sets
senses.definitionCN: 不同集合元素之间的匹配或对应
senses.example: There is a correlation between income and education level.
senses.exampleCN: 收入与教育水平之间存在对应关系。
senses.why: Correlation here means the two groups tend to match or correspond.
senses.whyCN: 此处 correlation 意为两组趋于匹配或对应。

senses.title: An act of correlating
senses.definition: the act of establishing a relationship between things
senses.definitionCN: 在事物之间建立关系的行为
senses.example: The correlation of the two data sets took weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 把两组数据关联起来花了数周。
senses.why: Correlation can name the act of finding the relationship, not just the relationship itself.
senses.whyCN: correlation 可以命名发现关系的行为，而不仅是关系本身。

senses.title: A reciprocal or complementary link
senses.definition: a reciprocal or complementary connection between things
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间互惠或互补的联系
senses.example: There is a correlation between supply and demand.
senses.exampleCN: 供需之间存在互补联系。
senses.why: When two things balance or complete each other, they show correlation.
senses.whyCN: 当两事物平衡或互补时，它们表现出 correlation。

senses.title: A pattern of co-occurrence
senses.definition: a pattern in which two things tend to appear or happen together
senses.definitionCN: 两事物倾向于一起出现或发生的模式
senses.example: Researchers noted a correlation between poverty and crime.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员注意到贫困与犯罪之间存在共现模式。
senses.why: Correlation can simply mean 'these things tend to go together', without claiming why.
senses.whyCN: correlation 可以仅表示「这些事物倾向于一起出现」，不声称原因。

senses.title: In grammar, a paired relationship
senses.definition: in grammar, a relationship between two words or clauses that work together
senses.definitionCN: 语法中，两个词或从句协同工作的关系
senses.example: 'Either...or' is a correlative conjunction.
senses.exampleCN: either...or 是关联连词。
senses.why: In grammar, correlatives are paired elements that depend on each other.
senses.whyCN: 在语法中，correlatives 是相互依赖的配对成分。

intro.en: Correlation is cor- (com-) + relation. Relation comes from Latin relatio, from referre 'to carry back'. The core is two things having a relation together.
intro.cn: correlation 是 cor-（com-）+ relation。relation 来自拉丁 relatio，relatio 源自 referre「带回」。核心是两事物一起具有关系。

items.en: ferre meant 'to carry'. referre is re- 'back' + ferre, meaning 'to carry back, relate'.
items.cn: ferre 意为「携带」。referre 是 re-「回」+ ferre，意为「带回、联系」。

items.en: relatio meant 'a bringing back, a relation, a report'.
items.cn: relatio 意为「带回、关系、报告」。

items.en: cor- is a form of com- 'together' used before r. correlation is 'a relation together'.
items.cn: cor- 是 com-「一起」在 r 前的形式。correlation 是「一起的关系」。

items.en: correlation = cor- + relation, formed in English or from Late Latin correlatio.
items.cn: correlation = cor- + relation，在英语中构成或来自后期拉丁 correlatio。

items.en: Correlation entered English in the 16th century, originally meaning 'a mutual relation'.
items.cn: correlation 在 16 世纪进入英语，最初意为「相互关系」。

items.en: The statistical sense developed in the 19th century with the work of Galton and Pearson.
items.cn: 统计义发展于 19 世纪，得益于高尔顿和皮尔逊的工作。

note.en: The first group shares ferre; the second contains near-synonyms for connection.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ferre；第二组是联系的近义词。

entries.definition: to have a mutual relationship; the verb behind correlation
entries.definitionCN: 具有相互关系；correlation 背后的动词

entries.definition: a connection between things; from relatio
entries.definitionCN: 事物之间的联系；来自 relatio

entries.definition: considered in relation to something else; from relatio
a relationship between things; broader than correlation
entries.definitionCN: 事物之间的关系；比 correlation 更广

entries.definition: a connection between ideas or things; close to correlation
entries.definitionCN: 观念或事物之间的联系；接近 correlation

entries.definition: the way things are connected; broader than correlation
entries.definitionCN: 事物联系方式；比 correlation 更广

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: cor- 'together' + relation: correlation is a relation two things have together.
normal.cn: cor-「一起」+ relation：correlation 是两事物一起具有的关系。

normal.en: correlate is the verb; correlation is the noun of the relationship.
normal.cn: correlate 是动词；correlation 是关系的名词。

normal.en: Correlation does not imply causation: things can vary together without one causing the other.
normal.cn: 相关不意味着因果：事物可以一起变化而无因果关系。

normal.en: A positive correlation means both go up together; negative means one up, one down.
normal.cn: 正相关意味着两者同升；负相关意味着一升一降。

normal.en: relation is the base; correlation adds cor- to emphasize the mutual link.
normal.cn: relation 是基础；correlation 加 cor- 强调相互联系。

abstract.en: Think of two dancers moving in sync: their movements show correlation.
abstract.cn: 想象两个舞者同步移动：他们的动作显示出 correlation。

abstract.en: Think of two lines on a graph that rise and fall together: that is correlation.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上两条同升同降的线：那就是 correlation。

abstract.en: Think of 'co-' meaning together: correlation = relation together.
abstract.cn: 把 co- 想成「一起」：correlation = 一起的关系。

examples.en: Scientists found a correlation between sleep and productivity.
examples.cn: 科学家发现睡眠与生产力之间存在关联。

examples.en: The correlation coefficient was 0.8, indicating a strong relationship.
examples.cn: 相关系数为 0.8，表明存在强相关关系。

examples.en: There is a high correlation between education level and income.
examples.cn: 教育水平与收入之间存在高度相关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠瑞雷神」——靠（cor-）着关系（relation）一起走 → correlation 关联

root: 拉丁 referre「带回、联系」（re-「回」+ ferre「携带」）→ relatio「关系」+ cor-（com-「一起」）→ correlation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'a relation two things share': statistical, causal, matching, or grammatical.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「两事物共享的关系」：统计的、因果的、匹配的或语法的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines on a graph rising and falling together.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表上两条同升同降的线。

branches.en: GENERAL RELATIONSHIP: a connection between things.
branches.cn: 一般关系：事物之间的联系。

branches.en: STATISTICAL CORRELATION: a quantified measure of co-variation.
branches.cn: 统计相关：共变的量化度量。

branches.en: MATCHING OR COMPLEMENTARY: sets or forces that correspond.
branches.cn: 匹配或互补：相对应的集合或力量。

branches.en: ACT OF CORRELATING: the process of linking things.
branches.cn: 关联行为：把事物联系起来的过程。

branches.en: CO-OCCURRENCE OR GRAMMAR: things that appear together or pair up.
branches.cn: 共现或语法：一起出现或配对的事物。

intro.en: Correlation is cor- (com-) + relation. The prefix cor- is fossilized; relation comes from Latin relatio (referre).
intro.cn: correlation 是 cor-（com-）+ relation。前缀 cor- 已凝固；relation 来自拉丁 relatio（referre）。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre 'to carry' produced refer, relate, relation, transfer, defer, infer, offer. Root: fer-/lat-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ferre「携带」产生了 refer、relate、relation、transfer、defer、infer、offer。词根：fer-/lat-。

definition_zh: 相符；通信；相当于
definition_en: to match or agree with something, to exchange letters, or to be equivalent to something
core_image: 两封信在邮路上相对而行，信里的字句一模一样
scene: 两张地图摊在桌上，河的弯道一处接一处地对上了。The two maps correspond at every bend of the river.
sceneCN: 这里 correspond 指「相符」（第 1 个义项：彼此一致）；句意是两张地图在河的每个弯道处都吻合。

senses.title: To match
senses.definition: to be similar to or in agreement with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相似或一致
senses.example: His account corresponds with the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与事实相符。
senses.why: Two shapes laid over each other show at once whether they fit.
senses.whyCN: 两个形状叠在一起，立刻就能看出是否吻合。

senses.title: To exchange letters
senses.definition: to write letters to someone and receive letters from them
senses.definitionCN: 给某人写信并收到对方的来信
senses.example: They corresponded for ten years before they met.
senses.exampleCN: 他们通信十年后才见面。
senses.why: A letter is an answer that travels a long way to arrive.
senses.whyCN: 一封信就是一个走了很远路才到达的回答。

senses.title: To be equivalent
senses.definition: to be the same as or to represent something else
senses.definitionCN: 等同于或代表另一事物
senses.example: This word corresponds to a short phrase in English.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词相当于英语里的一个短语。
senses.why: Two languages keep separate rooms for the same meaning.
senses.whyCN: 两种语言为同一个意思各留了一间房。

intro.en: Correspond joins Latin com-, together, and respondere, to answer, so it first meant to answer in turn.
intro.cn: correspond 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）组合，本指轮流作答。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer one another.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此应答。

items.en: Old French correspondre kept the sense of answering in turn.
items.cn: 古法语 correspondre 保留了轮流应答的意思。

items.en: English correspond added the sense of fitting or matching.
items.cn: 英语 correspond 增加了吻合、相符的意思。

items.en: It now covers matching facts, swapping letters and equal values.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖事实相符、书信往来与数值相当。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other words for matching and writing.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他表示吻合与通信的说法。

senses.example: The chart shows the correspondence between sounds and symbols.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表显示了声音与符号之间的对应关系。
senses.why: Every key needs its own lock, and every sign its own meaning.
senses.whyCN: 每把钥匙都要有自己的锁，每个符号都要有自己的意思。

intro.en: Correspondence comes from Latin correspondere, to answer one another, from com-, together, and respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondence 来自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or give a promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer each other in turn.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此轮流应答。

items.en: Old French kept the word for an exchange of answers.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个词，指回答的往来。

items.en: English correspondence named the exchange of letters.
items.cn: 英语 correspondence 指书信的往来。

items.en: It also names any tight fit between two sets of things.
items.cn: 它也表示两组事物之间严密的吻合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other words for letters and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他表示书信与一致的说法。

entries.definition: to match or exchange letters
a reporter or a person who writes letters
matching in position or meaning
written messages sent by post
entries.definitionCN: 通过邮局寄出的书面信息

entries.definition: the state of having the same view
a thing that fits or equals another
entries.definitionCN: 与另一物相配或相等的事物

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a box of old letters, then move to two reports that agree and to a table of paired signs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一盒旧信开始，再到两份一致的报告，最后到一张成对的符号表。

normal.en: Correspond is to answer back, and -ence makes it the whole exchange.
normal.cn: correspond 是回信，加 -ence 就成了整场往来。

normal.en: A correspondence can be a box of letters or a perfect fit.
normal.cn: correspondence 可以是一箱信，也可以是严丝合缝。

normal.en: Two people keep up a correspondence; two facts show correspondence.
normal.cn: 两个人保持通信，两件事则显示出一致。

normal.en: The ending -ence is the same one you hear in difference.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ence 与 difference 里的那个一样。

normal.en: A correspondence course travels by post instead of by bus.
normal.cn: 函授课程靠邮路而不是靠公交车来上课。

abstract.en: Picture two pens dipping into one inkwell, years apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两支笔隔着多年，蘸进同一只墨水瓶。

abstract.en: Picture two maps with every river drawn in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象两张地图把每条河都画在同一个位置。

abstract.en: Picture a row of keys facing a row of locks.
abstract.cn: 想象一排钥匙正对着一排锁。

examples.en: Their correspondence lasted more than twenty years.
examples.cn: 他们的通信持续了二十多年。

examples.en: There is a close correspondence between the two reports.
examples.cn: 这两份报告高度一致。

examples.en: She keeps her business correspondence in a grey box.
examples.cn: 她把商业信函放在一只灰色的盒子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correspondence 记成 correspond（互相回应）加 ence：彼此回应的东西，就是通信与一致。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，本指互相回应，后指书信往来与彼此一致。

sensesIntro.en: From letters answering each other, to reports that agree, and at last to signs paired with meanings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从彼此回应的书信，到互相一致的报告，最后到符号与意义的成对关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden box packed with letters that travelled both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木盒塞满来回旅行过的信。

branches.en: Two writers keep answering across the distance.
branches.cn: 两位写信人隔着距离不断回应。

branches.en: Two accounts of one event fit without a gap.
branches.cn: 同一事件的两种说法严丝合缝。

branches.en: Each sign on one side faces one sign on the other.
branches.cn: 一边的每个符号都对着另一边的某个符号。

branches.en: Letters and reports both aim at a meeting of two sides.
branches.cn: 书信与报告都指向两方的会合。

branches.en: Agreement in meaning and pairing in form are cousins.
branches.cn: 意思上的一致与形式上的配对是近亲。

intro.en: Correspondence is correspond plus the noun ending -ence, from Latin respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondence 由 correspond 加名词词尾 -ence 构成，源于拉丁语 respondere（回答）。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also runs through response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也贯穿 response、responsible 与 sponsor。

items.meaning: an exchange of answers or letters

definition_zh: 记者；通讯员；通信者；对应物
definition_en: a reporter based in a particular place, or a person who writes letters
core_image: 一个人蹲在战壕边，对着电话把远处的火光说给编辑部
scene: 战地记者蹲在掩体后，用卫星电话向编辑部口述现场。The correspondent sent her report from the border.
sceneCN: 这里 correspondent 指「派驻记者」（第 1 个义项：被派往某地报道的人）；句意是这位记者从边境发回了报道。

pos.zh: 记者；通讯员；通信者；对应物

senses.title: A reporter in the field
senses.definition: a journalist who reports from a particular place or on a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或就某专题发回报道的新闻工作者
senses.example: The correspondent sent her report from the border.
senses.exampleCN: 这位记者从边境发回了报道。
senses.why: News needs a pair of eyes that live where the story lives.
senses.whyCN: 新闻需要一双住在其发生地的眼睛。

senses.title: A person who writes letters
senses.definition: someone who exchanges letters with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人互相写信的人
senses.example: She has been a faithful correspondent for years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来她一直是个忠实的通信者。
senses.why: A letter is a visit that waits quietly in the post box.
senses.whyCN: 一封信就是一次拜访，静静等在信箱里。

senses.title: A matching counterpart
senses.definition: a thing that matches or corresponds to another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相匹配或相对应的事物
senses.example: This verb is the correspondent of that noun.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词是那个名词的对应形式。
senses.why: Two forms of one meaning stand facing each other.
senses.whyCN: 同一个意思的两种形式，面对面站着。

intro.en: Correspondent is the person noun from correspond, built on Latin correspondere, to answer one another.
intro.cn: correspondent 是 correspond 的人物名词，源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答）。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer one another.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此应答。

items.en: The noun named someone who answers or writes.
items.cn: 这个名词指作答或写信的人。

items.en: English correspondent came to mean a writer of news from far away.
items.cn: 英语 correspondent 逐渐指从远方写回新闻的人。

items.en: It now names both reporters and steady letter writers.
items.cn: 今天它既指记者，也指长期通信的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other people who report or write.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他报道或写信的人。

entries.definition: to match or exchange letters
letters exchanged or a close match
related one to one
a person who gathers and reports news
a person who writes for newspapers or magazines
entries.definitionCN: 为报纸或杂志写作的人

entries.definition: a friend known only through letters
entries.definitionCN: 只通过书信交往的朋友

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a voice calling from a distant border, then move to a steady letter writer and to a matching form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从远方边境传来的声音开始，再到忠实的写信人，最后到相对应的形式。

normal.en: A correspondent answers the world with a report.
normal.cn: 记者用一篇报道回应整个世界。

normal.en: The word ends in -ent, like agent and student, so it names a person.
normal.cn: 这个词以 -ent 结尾，像 agent 和 student，因此指人。

normal.en: A war correspondent carries a notebook where others carry a gun.
normal.cn: 战地记者带着笔记本，别人带着枪。

normal.en: A pen friend is a correspondent who never knocks at the door.
normal.cn: 笔友是一位从不上门敲门的通信者。

normal.en: If two forms match, each is the correspondent of the other.
normal.cn: 如果两种形式相配，彼此就是对方的对应物。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone held out toward a distant fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一支话筒伸向远处的火光。

abstract.en: Picture a letter arriving every winter without fail.
abstract.cn: 想象每年冬天都准时到达的一封信。

abstract.en: Picture two words standing face to face like mirrors.
abstract.cn: 想象两个词像镜子一样面对面站着。

examples.en: The correspondent sent her report from the border.
examples.cn: 这位记者从边境发回了报道。

examples.en: She has been a faithful correspondent for years.
examples.cn: 多年来她一直是个忠实的通信者。

examples.en: A foreign correspondent often works alone.
examples.cn: 驻外记者常常独自工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correspondent 记成 correspond（互相回应）加 ent（人）：替远方回应世界的人，就是记者与通信者。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，加上人物词尾 -ent，指回应与报道的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a reporter answering the world, to a letter writer answering a friend, and at last to a form answering another form.
sensesIntro.cn: 从回应世界的记者，到回应朋友的写信人，最后到回应另一种形式的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice at a distant border speaking into a telephone.
core.cn: 核心意象：远方边境的一个声音对着电话说话。

branches.en: The reporter stands where the news is happening.
branches.cn: 记者站在新闻正在发生的地方。

branches.en: The letter writer keeps a quiet conversation alive.
branches.cn: 写信人让一场安静的对话持续下去。

branches.en: A matching form answers another form one to one.
branches.cn: 对应的形式与另一形式逐一呼应。

branches.en: Both answer someone far away, one by news and one by letter.
branches.cn: 两者都在回应远方的人，一个用新闻，一个用书信。

branches.en: A steady writer and a matching form both keep a link unbroken.
branches.cn: 忠实的写信人与对应的形式，都让一条联系不断。

intro.en: Correspondent is correspond plus -ent, a person ending, from Latin respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondent 由 correspond 加人物词尾 -ent 构成，源于拉丁语 respondere（回答）。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also appears in response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也出现在 response、responsible 与 sponsor 中。

definition_zh: 走廊；过道；狭长地带
definition_en: a long narrow passage inside a building, or a narrow strip of land between two areas
core_image: 一条长长的通道，两侧的门一扇接一扇，尽头透进白光
scene: 医院三楼的走廊很长，尽头那扇窗透进一片白光。A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 corridor 指「走廊」（第 1 个义项：建筑物内连接房间的长通道）；句意是一位护士快步走过走廊。

collocations.phrase: at the end of the corridor

derivatives.zh: 信使；快递员（与 corridor 同源于「跑」）
光标（同源词，本指奔跑者）

senses.title: A passage inside a building
senses.definition: a long narrow passage that connects rooms in a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物内连接各个房间的狭长通道
senses.example: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一位护士快步走过走廊。
senses.why: A building needs a spine so that its rooms can be one body.
senses.whyCN: 建筑需要一根脊梁，房间才能连成一个身体。

senses.title: A strip of land
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大区域的狭长土地
senses.example: The road runs through a narrow corridor of land.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路穿过一条狭长地带。
senses.why: Countries also need passages, and they guard them like doors.
senses.whyCN: 国家也需要通道，并像守门一样守着它们。

senses.title: The aisle of a train
senses.definition: the narrow walking space between seats in a train or plane
senses.definitionCN: 火车或飞机座位之间供人行走的窄道
senses.example: He stood in the corridor with his ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿着车票站在车厢过道里。
senses.why: Even a moving box needs a line along which people pass.
senses.whyCN: 即使是一只移动的盒子，也需要一条让人通过的线。

intro.en: Corridor comes from Italian corridore, a runner or running place, from correre, to run, and Latin currere.
intro.cn: corridor 来自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），源自 correre（跑）与拉丁语 currere。

items.en: Currere meant to run.
items.cn: currere 意为奔跑。

items.en: Corridore named a runner or a place for running.
items.cn: corridore 指奔跑的人或供奔跑的地方。

items.en: French corridor named a narrow passage in a fortress.
items.cn: 法语 corridor 指堡垒中的狭窄通道。

items.en: English corridor first meant a covered walk or gallery.
items.cn: 英语 corridor 最初指有顶的步道或长廊。

items.en: It now means any long passage, in a building or on a map.
items.cn: 今天它指任何长通道，无论在大楼里还是地图上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the running base curr-, and the meaning group names other ways through a building.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示奔跑的词基 curr-，近义组列出其他穿过建筑的说法。

to drive animals into an enclosure
a ring of light around the sun
a passage just inside the front door
a narrow way from one place to another

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long passage lined with doors, then move to a narrow strip of land and to a train aisle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两侧都是门的长通道开始，再到狭长地带，最后到车厢过道。

normal.en: Corridor comes from a word for running, so it is a place made for moving.
normal.cn: corridor 源自表示奔跑的词，所以它是为移动而设的地方。

normal.en: A corridor has two rows of doors and no chairs.
normal.cn: 走廊有两排门，却没有椅子。

normal.en: Hospitals keep corridors long so that beds can pass.
normal.cn: 医院把走廊修得长，是为了让病床通过。

normal.en: A land corridor is a hallway between two countries.
normal.cn: 陆上走廊就是两国之间的一条过道。

normal.en: The double r in the middle keeps the word running.
normal.cn: 中间的两个 r 让这个词一直向前跑。

abstract.en: Picture a line of doors standing one behind another.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门一层层排在身后。

abstract.en: Picture a thin neck of land joining two wide rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细长的陆地，把两片宽阔的土地连起来。

abstract.en: Picture light at the far end of a very long tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条很长隧道的尽头有光。

examples.en: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
examples.cn: 一位护士快步走过走廊。

examples.en: Their office is at the end of the corridor.
examples.cn: 他们的办公室在走廊尽头。

examples.en: The train corridor was full of luggage.
examples.cn: 火车过道里堆满了行李。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 corridor 记成「能跑的道」：两侧是门、中间能一路跑到尽头，就是走廊。

root: 源自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），来自 correre（跑），再上溯到拉丁语 currere（奔跑），本指供人穿行的长道。

sensesIntro.en: From a passage between rooms, to a thin strip of land, and at last to the aisle of a moving carriage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从房间之间的通道，到一条细长的土地，最后到移动车厢里的过道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long narrow passage with doors on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长而窄的通道，两侧都是门。

branches.en: The corridor turns separate rooms into one building.
branches.cn: 走廊把一个个房间变成一栋完整的建筑。

branches.en: A narrow strip of land turns two areas into neighbours.
branches.cn: 一条狭长土地把两片区域变成邻居。

branches.en: An aisle lets people pass while the carriage moves.
branches.cn: 过道让人们在车厢移动时仍能通行。

branches.en: Both are thin lines that join larger spaces.
branches.cn: 两者都是连接较大空间的细线。

branches.en: Land corridor and train aisle are both narrow routes of passage.
branches.cn: 陆上走廊与车厢过道都是狭窄的通行路线。

intro.en: Corridor is built on Latin currere, to run, through Italian corridore, a running place.
intro.cn: corridor 建立在拉丁语 currere（奔跑）之上，经意大利语 corridore（跑道）而来。

latinIntro.en: The running base curr- also appears in current, cursor and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示奔跑的词基 curr- 也出现在 current、cursor 与 excursion 中。

items.exampleCN: 这趟走廊式列车逢站就停。

items.meaning: a carriage with a side passage

definition_zh: 腐蚀；侵蚀；逐渐破坏；削弱
definition_en: to eat away a material or gradually destroy something, often by chemical action
core_image: 一块铁在盐水里放了一夜，表面浮起红褐色的鳞片，手一碰就掉渣
scene: 桥梁检查报告指出，海风与盐雾正在慢慢吃掉钢梁。Salt spray had corroded the bridge supports.
sceneCN: 这里 corrode 指盐雾化学性地侵蚀金属（第 1 个义项：腐蚀材料）；句意为盐雾已经腐蚀了桥墩。

senses.title: Eat away metal
senses.definition: of a chemical, to destroy metal slowly by oxidation or acid action
senses.definitionCN: 指化学物质通过氧化或酸作用缓慢毁坏金属
senses.example: Salt spray had corroded the bridge supports.
senses.exampleCN: 盐雾已经腐蚀了桥墩。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to gnaw': acid gnaws at metal the way teeth gnaw at a bone.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「啃咬」：酸啃金属，正如牙齿啃骨头。

senses.title: Attack a surface
senses.definition: to wear away the surface of a material
senses.definitionCN: 磨损材料表面
senses.example: The acid corroded the marble floor.
senses.exampleCN: 酸侵蚀了大理石地面。
senses.why: Surface is where the attack becomes visible; the damage begins at the boundary and works inward.
senses.whyCN: 表面是攻击变得可见的地方；损坏从边界开始，向内推进。

senses.title: Destroy gradually
senses.definition: to destroy something slowly and piece by piece
senses.definitionCN: 一点一点地缓慢毁坏某物
senses.example: Neglect had corroded the old machine beyond repair.
senses.exampleCN: 疏于维护使旧机器损坏到无法修理。
senses.why: Anything left exposed will be eaten away by something; neglect is simply exposure without protection.
senses.whyCN: 任何暴露在外的东西都会被害虫般的因素吃掉；疏于维护不过是无保护的暴露。

senses.title: Undermine trust
senses.definition: to weaken confidence, trust or morale over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间削弱信心、信任或士气
senses.example: Repeated delays corroded trust between the two teams.
senses.exampleCN: 反复延误侵蚀了两个团队之间的信任。
senses.why: Trust is a surface that holds relationships; once it is eaten through, the structure fails.
senses.whyCN: 信任是托住关系的表面；一旦被蛀穿，结构就崩塌。

senses.title: Deteriorate on its own
senses.definition: of a material, to become degraded through time and exposure
senses.definitionCN: 指材料随时间与暴露而退化
senses.example: The pipes corroded faster in the damp basement.
senses.exampleCN: 管道在潮湿的地下室里腐蚀得更快。
senses.why: The verb can drop its agent: the metal does not need to be attacked, it only needs the wrong conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以省略施事者：金属不必被谁攻击，只要条件不对，它自己就会坏。

senses.title: Dissolve rock by acid
senses.definition: of acid water, to dissolve or wear rock
senses.definitionCN: 指酸性水溶解或磨损岩石
senses.example: Acid rain corroded the limestone statues.
senses.exampleCN: 酸雨腐蚀了石灰岩雕像。
senses.why: Limestone is soft enough for weak acid to eat it, so geology repeats the same gnawing at a slower pace.
senses.whyCN: 石灰岩足够软，弱酸就能吃掉它，于是地质过程以更慢的节奏重复同样的啃咬。

senses.title: Erode moral values
senses.definition: to weaken moral standards or principles
senses.definitionCN: 削弱道德标准或原则
senses.example: Cynicism can corrode a community's shared values.
senses.exampleCN: 犬儒心态会侵蚀一个社群共享的价值。
senses.why: Shared values hold a group together the way metal holds a bridge; the loss is slow, then structural.
senses.whyCN: 共享价值像金属托住桥梁那样托住一个群体；损失先是缓慢的，随后是结构性的。

senses.title: Consume little by little
senses.definition: to consume or reduce something gradually, as if by gnawing
senses.definitionCN: 像啃咬那样逐渐消耗或减少某物
senses.example: Debt corroded the family's savings year by year.
senses.exampleCN: 债务年复一年地吞噬这个家庭的储蓄。
senses.why: The gnawing image survives in abstract losses: nothing is taken at once, and that is what makes it dangerous.
senses.whyCN: 「啃咬」的意象在抽象的损失中延续：没有东西是一次被拿走的，而这正使它危险。

intro.en: Corrode comes from a Latin verb meaning to gnaw away, built from 'together' and 'gnaw'.
intro.cn: corrode 来自一个意为「啃掉」的拉丁动词，由「一起」与「啃」构成。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. for chemical eating of metals, and later used it for trust and values.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，指化学性侵蚀金属，后来用于信任与价值。

items.en: Corrodere meant 'to gnaw to pieces, eat away', from com- (intensive) and rodere 'to gnaw'.
items.cn: corrodere 意为「啃碎、吃掉」，由加强语气的前缀 com- 与 rodere「啃」构成。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' also gives rodent, the animal that gnaws, and erode through a related verb.
items.cn: rodere「啃」也产生 rodent（啃咬的动物），并通过相关动词产生 erode。

items.en: Corrosio named the gnawing away, and English corrosion followed the same pattern.
items.cn: corrosio 命名啃蚀，英语 corrosion 沿用同一模式。

items.en: Chemistry gave the word its precise sense, and moral writing borrowed it for anything slowly eaten from within.
items.cn: 化学给了这个词精确含义，道德写作则借它指任何被从内部慢慢吃掉的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gnawing root; the near-meaning group names kinds of wearing away.
note.cn: 形近组共享「啃」词根；近义组列出各种磨损。

entries.definitionCN: 逐渐磨损，尤指被风或水。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of acid gnawing at metal.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「酸啃金属」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think of teeth: corrode means to gnaw away, only the teeth are acid.
normal.cn: 想想牙齿：corrode 就是啃掉，只不过牙齿换成了酸。

normal.en: Salt water on iron leaves red flakes; that is corrosion at work.
normal.cn: 盐水泡铁留下红色鳞片，那就是腐蚀在工作。

normal.en: Trust can be corroded the way metal is: slowly, from the surface in.
normal.cn: 信任像金属一样会被腐蚀：缓慢地，从表面向内。

normal.en: Say cor-RODE, with the stress on the gnawing.
normal.cn: 读成 cor-RODE，重音落在「啃咬」上。

normal.en: Link it with rodent: both words are about gnawing.
normal.cn: 把它和 rodent 联系：两个词都与啃咬有关。

abstract.en: Nothing is taken at once, which is why corrosion is easy to ignore.
abstract.cn: 没有东西是一次被拿走的，所以腐蚀容易被忽视。

abstract.en: A structure fails at the surface before it fails at the core.
abstract.cn: 结构先在表面失效，再在核心失效。

abstract.en: The same verb serves metal, trust and values because all three are eaten from within.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词适用于金属、信任与价值，因为三者都是从内部被吃掉。

examples.en: Salt spray had corroded the bridge supports.
examples.cn: 盐雾已经腐蚀了桥墩。

examples.en: Repeated delays corroded trust between the two teams.
examples.cn: 反复延误侵蚀了两个团队之间的信任。

examples.en: Acid rain corroded the limestone statues.
examples.cn: 酸雨腐蚀了石灰岩雕像。
